local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 each of Connecticut's 54 probate districts elects its judge of probate for four years, and the towns whose registrars of voters are up elect them (registrars serve two years from each state election unless a town has chosen four-year terms); both offices are on the state election ballot with party lines. Connecticut has no county government, so no county office is elected. Selectmen, mayors, councils, town clerks, boards of education and other town officers are chosen at municipal elections in odd-numbered years, in November or in May, so they are not on this ballot unless a town's own charter or a vacancy puts one there.
local_calendar.s: Connecticut General Statutes sections 45a-18 (judges of probate), 9-190, 9-190a and 9-189a (registrars of voters), and 9-164 and 9-185 (municipal elections and town officers)

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Secretary of the State's sample ballots, one per town: 19 of the 169 towns' ballots were posted when the list was read on September 30, 2026. They give the judge of probate contest of 16 of the 54 probate districts (19 candidates; every posted town of a district must print the same names) and the registrar of voters contest of 17 towns (31 candidates). The other 38 probate districts have no town posted yet and are listed without candidates until one is. The ballot of Canaan prints the registrar's office with no candidate's name, and the contest is shown with none. The ballots of Coventry and Harwinton print no registrar of voters column. Not loaded: registered write-in candidates, who are not printed on a ballot; ballot questions; and any other town office a ballot prints (none of the posted ballots prints one). A ballot prints no withdrawn candidate, so none can be counted. Towns are filed under Connecticut's eight counties, which have no government but still say where a town lies; the Census Bureau's newer planning regions are not used.
local_coverage.s: Connecticut Secretary of the State, November 3, 2026, State Election, Sample Town Ballots; Connecticut General Statutes section 45a-2 (the towns of each probate district); U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 county subdivision codes (towns and counties)

gaps.w: judge of probate and registrar of voters candidates in towns whose ballot is not posted yet
gaps.r: The Secretary of the State posts each town's sample ballot as it is approved: 19 of the 169 towns' ballots were posted when the list was read on September 30, 2026. State law has every town's registrars of voters file the sample ballot at least ten days before early voting begins on October 19, so the rest are due by October 9 (C.G.S. 9-256 and 9-163aa); a town's candidates are loaded once its ballot is posted.
